note: Ps58 against unjust rulers (corrected; imprecatory, imagery-heavy). Human IB core: the rulers' hearts (seat) devising wrongs (paal/evel) + hands dealing out (palas) violence; the wicked estranged (zur) + astray (taah) from the womb, speaking lies (kazab); their venom (chemah) like a deaf adder that will not hear (shama = willful incorrigibility); the righteous rejoicing (samach) at God's vengeance. God-qualifiers=4 (break teeth, tear out fangs v6, vengeance v10, God who judges v11). The serpent/adder/teeth/fangs/lion/water/arrow/snail/stillborn/thorn imagery + the wished dissolution + the ruler-address (gods/decree/judge) = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: heart (leb - in your hearts you devise wrongs)
the seat where wrongs are devised

'No, in your HEARTS (leb) you devise wrongs' — the injustice traced to its inward source; leb here the rulers' hearts, where wrong is planned before the hands deal out violence — corruption at the seat of will, behind the show of judgment
'in your hearts you DEVISE (paal) wrongs' — the deliberate contriving of injustice; paal (to do/work) here the inner manufacture of wrong, calculated in the heart — evil designed, not stumbled into
paired with the violence dealt out

'you devise WRONGS (evel)' — the injustice that is the rulers' true product; evel (unrighteousness/iniquity) the wrong their hearts plan — the opposite of the 'righteousness' they were meant to decree (v1)
weigh out / deal out (palas - your hands deal out violence)
as if weighing it out deliberately

'your hands DEAL OUT (palas) violence on earth' — the inner wrong made outward; palas (to weigh/mete out) the rulers dispensing violence as if measuring justice — the hands executing what the heart devised, a grim parody of judgment
the outward form of the wrongs devised

'your hands deal out VIOLENCE (chamas) on earth' — the harvest of the corrupt heart; chamas (violent wrong, cf Ps55) the cruelty the rulers spread abroad — injustice not merely thought but inflicted on the land
wicked (rasha - the wicked are estranged from the womb)
paired with going astray and speaking lies
whose fangs God is asked to break (v6)

'The WICKED (rasha) are estranged from the womb' — the godless traced to their very origin; rasha here the wicked whose corruption is innate, not acquired — the enemies whose venomous teeth God is asked to break (v6)
be estranged / alienated (zur - estranged from the womb)
be estranged / go one's own way
paired with going astray from birth

'the wicked are ESTRANGED (zur) from the womb' — alienation from the good present at birth; zur (to be a stranger/turn aside) the innate estrangement of the wicked, foreign to righteousness from the start — a depravity as old as they are (cf Ps51:5)
go astray / err (taah - they go astray from birth)
paired with being estranged from the womb

'they GO ASTRAY (taah) from birth, speaking lies' — the erring that begins at birth; taah (to wander/go astray) the wicked's early and lifelong deviation from truth, expressed at once in lying speech — corruption that talks from the cradle
the immediate fruit of going astray from birth

'they go astray from birth, speaking LIES (kazab)' — falsehood as the native tongue of the wicked; kazab (lies/deception) the speech that betrays their inborn estrangement — untruth issuing from a heart astray from the start
like the venom of a serpent, a deaf adder
paired with the willful refusal to hear (v5)

'They have VENOM (chemah) like the venom of a serpent' — malice as deadly poison; chemah (heat/venom/wrath) the wicked's inner toxicity, likened to a serpent's — and worse, a deaf adder that will not be charmed (v5), venom joined to incorrigibility
hear / heed (shama - does not hear the charmers)
the voice of charmers / the cunning enchanter

'so that it does not HEAR (shama) the voice of charmers' — the willful, self-stopped deafness of the wicked; shama here refused, the adder stopping its own ear against any charm — the wicked's incorrigibility, deaf to all correction and appeal (contrast the fearless who hear God's word, Ps56)
issues in rejoicing at the vengeance

'The RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq) will rejoice when he sees the vengeance' — the upright vindicated at last; tsaddiq the God-fearing whose faith is confirmed when justice falls on the wicked — the counterpart to the corrupt rulers, at whose downfall he rejoices
rejoice / be glad (samach - the righteous will rejoice)
at seeing God's vengeance on the wicked
the response of the righteous to vengeance
because there is a God who judges on earth (v11)

'the righteous will REJOICE (samach) when he sees the vengeance' — joy not in cruelty but in justice done; samach here the gladness that God's moral order holds — 'surely there is a God who judges on earth' (v11, the qualifier) — vindication answering long injustice
break / tear down (haras - break the teeth in their mouths)
God asked to break the wicked's teeth (v6)

v6 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'O God, BREAK (haras) the teeth in their mouths' - God's judgment is not a human IB char; the imprecation the psalmist prays against the wicked (280483), disarming their venomous bite. Qualifier.
tear out / break down (nathats - tear out the fangs)
God asked to tear out the fangs of the young lions (v6)

v6 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'TEAR OUT (nathats) the fangs of the young lions, O LORD!' - God's judgment is not a human IB char; the second imprecation against the predatory wicked (280483). Qualifier.
vengeance / retribution (naqam - he sees the vengeance)
God's vengeance, at which the righteous rejoice (v10)
v10 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'when he sees the VENGEANCE (naqam)' - God's retribution on the wicked is not a human IB char; the just judgment the righteous rejoice to witness (280456). Qualifier.
judge (shaphat - a God who judges on earth)
there is a God who judges the earth, ground of the righteous' joy (v11)

v11 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'surely there is a God who JUDGES (shaphat) on earth' - God's judging is not a human IB char; the affirmed moral order that grounds the righteous' reward and joy (280456) - the true Judge over against the failed human 'gods' (v1). Qualifier.
speak / decree (dabar - do you decree what is right?)

v1: 'Do you indeed DECREE (dabar) what is right, you gods?' - the rulers' pronouncing of judgment, challenged; their injustice is the char (v2), here the bare judicial act questioned. Standalone (the rulers' act).

v1: 'do you decree what is RIGHT (tsedeq)?' - the righteousness the rulers were meant to administer but fail to; the standard violated (their wrong-devising is the char, v2). Standalone (the justice-standard failed).
v1: 'you GODS (elem)?' - the human rulers/judges addressed by their exalted title (perhaps ironically); the persons challenged, whose corruption is read in v2. Standalone (the rulers addressed).

v1: 'Do you JUDGE (shaphat) the children of man uprightly?' - the rulers' judging function, challenged; their failure of it is the theme, the injustice captured in v2. Standalone (the judging function).
v1: 'do you judge UPRIGHTLY (meshar)?' - the equity the rulers owe but withhold; the standard they violate, their wrongs the char (v2). Standalone (the standard failed).

v3: 'estranged from the WOMB (rechem)' - the point of origin marking the wicked's innate corruption; the temporal 'from birth', its content carried in the estranged/astray chars (280484,280487). Standalone (origin marker).
v3: 'they go astray from birth, SPEAKING (dabar) lies' - the act of speaking; its content, lies, is the char (280491), here the bare verb of utterance. Standalone (the speaking).
likeness / like (demut - like the venom of a serpent)
v4: 'venom LIKE (demut) the venom of a serpent' - the comparison particle introducing the serpent-simile for the wicked's venom (280492). Standalone (simile marker).
venom (chemah - the venom of a serpent)
v4: 'like the VENOM (chemah) of a serpent' - the serpent's poison, the simile-vehicle for the wicked's malice (the char, 280492). Standalone (simile vehicle).
serpent (nachash - like the venom of a serpent)
v4: 'the venom of a SERPENT (nachash)' - the snake-image for the wicked's poison; part of the venom-simile. Standalone (image).
v4: 'like the DEAF (cheresh) adder' - the deafness of the adder imaging the wicked's willful refusal to hear (the char, 280502). Standalone (image).
v4: 'the deaf ADDER (pethen)' - the cobra-image for the wicked's poisonous incorrigibility; part of the serpent-simile. Standalone (image).
v4: 'the deaf adder that STOPS (atam) its ear' - the image of the snake shutting its own ear; the willful deafness it pictures is the char (280502). Standalone (image of self-stopping).
v5: 'does not hear the VOICE (qol) of charmers' - the charmer's voice the adder ignores; part of the deaf-adder simile, the appeal the wicked refuse (char 280502). Standalone (image).
v5: 'the voice of CHARMERS (lachash)' - the snake-charmers whose voice the deaf adder ignores; the simile-figure for those who would correct the wicked. Standalone (image).
v5: 'the CUNNING (chakam) enchanter' - the skilled charmer whose art the adder resists; a quality of the simile-figure (the charmer), not a disposition of the wicked. Standalone (image detail).
enchanter / binder of spells (chaber - the cunning enchanter)
v5: 'the cunning ENCHANTER (chaber)' - the spell-binding charmer the adder will not heed; part of the deaf-adder simile. Standalone (image).
teeth (shen - break the teeth in their mouths)
v6: 'break the TEETH (shen) in their mouths' - the wicked's teeth as their weapon of harm; the object of God's breaking (qualifier 306392). Standalone (image).
mouth (peh - the teeth in their mouths)
v6: 'the teeth in their MOUTHS (peh)' - the mouth as the site of the wicked's biting menace; part of the break-the-teeth imprecation. Standalone (image).
fangs / great teeth (malteah - tear out the fangs)
v6: 'tear out the FANGS (malteah) of the young lions' - the predatory fangs of the wicked; the object of God's tearing-out (qualifier 306395). Standalone (image).
young lions (kephir - the fangs of the young lions)
v6: 'the fangs of the YOUNG LIONS (kephir)' - the wicked imaged as predatory young lions; the beast-figure of their menace. Standalone (image).
melt / vanish (maas - let them vanish like water)
v7: 'Let them VANISH (maas) like water that runs away' - the wished dissolution of the wicked; the imprecation's outcome (their melting away), not a disposition. Standalone (wished fate).
water (mayim - like water that runs away)
v7: 'like WATER (mayim) that runs away' - the image of the wicked draining away to nothing; part of the wished-dissolution simile. Standalone (image).
go / run away (halak - water that runs away)
v7: 'water that RUNS AWAY (halak)' - the flowing-off of the water, imaging the wicked's disappearance; part of the dissolution-simile. Standalone (image).
aim / bend the bow (darak - when he aims his arrows)
v7: 'when he AIMS (darak) his arrows, let them be blunted' - the wicked drawing the bow, their weapon rendered useless; part of the imprecation. Standalone (image).
v7: 'when he aims his ARROWS (chets)' - the wicked's arrows, wished blunted; part of the disarming imprecation. Standalone (image).
be blunted / cut off (malal - let them be blunted)
v7: 'let them be BLUNTED (malal)' - the wished blunting of the wicked's arrows; the imprecation's outcome, disarming their attack. Standalone (wished fate).
v8: 'like the SNAIL (shablul) that dissolves into slime' - the image of the wicked wasting away; part of the wished-dissolution catalogue. Standalone (image).
v8: 'that DISSOLVES (temes) into slime' - the snail melting to slime, imaging the wicked's disappearance; part of the dissolution-simile. Standalone (image).
v8: 'dissolves into SLIME (temes)' - the trail of the melting snail, image of the wicked coming to nothing; part of the simile. Standalone (image).
stillborn / miscarriage (nephel - like the stillborn child)
v8: 'like the STILLBORN (nephel) child who never sees the sun' - the image of the wicked as one who never sees light; part of the wished-dissolution catalogue. Standalone (image).
see / behold (chazah - who never sees the sun)
v8: 'who never SEES (chazah) the sun' - the stillborn never beholding daylight, imaging the wicked's non-being; part of the simile. Standalone (image).
v8: 'who never sees the SUN (shemesh)' - the daylight the stillborn never sees; part of the dissolution-simile. Standalone (image).
v9: 'Sooner than your POTS (sir) can feel the heat of thorns' - the cooking-pots in the obscure sweeping-away image; part of the imprecation's picture of sudden judgment. Standalone (image).
perceive / feel (bin - before your pots can feel)

v9: 'before your pots CAN FEEL (bin) the heat of thorns' - the pots sensing the fire, part of the 'sooner than' image of sudden judgment; not an inner operation of the wicked or righteous. Standalone (image detail).
v9: 'the heat of THORNS (atad)' - the thorn-fire under the pots, image of the swift judgment; part of the obscure sweeping-away picture. Standalone (image).
burning / ablaze (charon - whether green or ablaze)
v9: 'whether green or ABLAZE (charon)' - the thorns whether fresh or burning, part of the sudden-judgment image; not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
sweep away (saar - may he sweep them away)
v9: 'may he sweep them AWAY (saar)' - the wished sudden removal of the wicked (as by a whirlwind); the imprecation's outcome, not a disposition. Standalone (wished fate).
see / behold (chazah - when he sees the vengeance)
v10: 'the righteous will rejoice when he SEES (chazah) the vengeance' - the righteous witnessing God's judgment; the seeing that occasions his joy (the char, 280456). Standalone (the beholding).
bathe / wash (rachats - bathe his feet in the blood)

v10: 'he will BATHE (rachats) his feet in the blood of the wicked' - the vivid symbol of the righteous' total vindication over the fallen wicked; a figure of triumph, the joy carried in the rejoice char (280456). Standalone (vindication symbol).
blood (dam - the blood of the wicked)
v10: 'in the BLOOD (dam) of the wicked' - the slaughter of the wicked, image of their judgment; the medium of the vindication-symbol. Standalone (image).
wicked (rasha - the blood of the wicked)
v10: 'the blood of the WICKED (rasha)' - the wicked now judged; their character is the char (v3, 280483), here the judged object of the vengeance. Standalone (the judged wicked).
fruit / reward (peri - a reward for the righteous)
v11: 'Surely there is a REWARD (peri) for the righteous' - the vindication/recompense mankind acknowledges the righteous receive; the moral-order outcome, not a disposition. Standalone (the reward).
righteous (tsaddiq - a reward for the righteous)

v11: 'a reward for the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq)' - the righteous in mankind's closing affirmation; their character is the char (v10, 280455), here the recipients of the reward in the moral-order statement. Standalone (the vindicated righteous).
